Why Join Risk Consulting at AIG? 

Risk Consulting at AIG is about teamwork! It is about utilizing your resources, working together to solve real world problems, and making a positive impact on our client’s futures. When asked, “why do we enjoy what we do?” The answer is simple, the people. 

The role of an Account Risk Engineer is critical to what we do at AIG, both as a risk management resource to our clients and as a leading global insurance organization. Account Risk Engineers are responsible for working with clients to identify and mitigate risks to their business such as fire, flood, windstorm, equipment breakdown etc. 

A Day in the Life 

Looking for variety and a challenge? Client’s range in size, scope and complexity. One day you may be discussing the loss prevention strategy on an account with an underwriter, the next, surveying a manufacturing plant or diving into the contingent business interruption risks of an account. The key to success isn’t about being the expert in every occupancy, it’s about building trust and cross-functional relationships with stakeholders through effective communication. You will tap into your strong analytical skills, utilize internal and external guidelines, and leading-edge tools and methodologies to develop your view of an accounts risk profile. Need that occupancy expertise after all? We have a Technical Integration Group as well as a vast team with years of experience to provide training, mentorship, and collaboration.

We offer flexible work hours, the ability to work from home; as well as many other company wide benefits like continued education and tuition reimbursement, 401(K), maternity/paternity leave, volunteer time off, and a strong sense of community! 

What You’ll Need 

Bachelor’s degree in Science, Technology, Engineering or Mathematics 

Minimum fifteen (15) years of highly protected risk, specialized industry and/or boiler and machinery field experience 

Knowledge of a wide range of light to high hazard occupancies and considered a subject matter expert in some

Strong communicator (both oral and written) 

Position is expected to travel and attend meetings at various office, field, and construction sites 

Job Responsibilities: 

Perform property loss prevention reviews of commercial property accounts

Document the account review results in a data-driven application

Conduct periodic client service meetings with underwriting, broker and client

Analyze and manage risk improvements of an account and work with the client to prioritize and implement them

Translate client needs and loss prevention strategies into a client service plan

Estimate of the cost of engineering services

Conduct reviews of field survey reports

Periodically conduct or witness property loss prevention surveys key facilities of a client

Technically analyze the loss prevention attributes of a facility including:

Determine building construction and assess the impact of plastics on construction

Analyze water supplies and sprinkler system demands to determine water supply and sprinkler system adequacy

Identify occupancy hazards and assess the adequacy of their protection features

Identify and assess the impact of external exposures on a facility

Determine fire and natural catastrophe loss estimates for a facility

Conduct consultative visits at customer facilities

Conduct plan reviews

Witness fire protection equipment testing

Provide engineering data system support/guidance and stay abreast of system related issues within region

Strengths for the position:

 Soft Skills:

Highly motivated and works well without close supervision.

The individual must be able to make decisions with and without established guidelines and to provide technical support to underwriters and clients. 

Ability to work closely with various Account Teams including Account Engineers and Underwriters 

Ability to complete assignments on-time.

Professional Engineer or Certified Fire Protection Specialist Designation (desired but not required). 

Ability to perform inspections of buildings and other structures, both visually and with instruments 

Ability to read construction drawings, diagrams, printed materials

Possess at minimum of at least one year of driving experience with a valid U.S. driver’s license

Ability to perform physical activities required for the position (i.e., be on feet and walking 8-10 hours a day, safely work at heights)

Ability to safely work in a variety of occupationally hazardous locations

Ability to type at a computer for several hours a day

Ability to drive and safely operate a motor vehicle

Participate in and lead zonal audits

Partner with the business to identify and analyze the inherent risks in Investments, FP&A and related Finance Processes and the controls that management has implemented to mitigate their risks.

Lead the Finance audits including SOX testing coverage to ensure that audit projects and stakeholders focus on key risks and controls.

Present audit findings, risk insights, and recommendations to senior management.

Educate stakeholders on the IAG process and work to improve the overall audit experience.

Contribute to the overall effectiveness and value of IAG by recommending and developing innovative approaches and solutions (e.g. the use of data analytics, automation, and Agile audit methodology)

Proactively identify and propose efficiencies and rationalization opportunities to stakeholders.

Multinational
AIG’s Multinational business is an exciting area within General Insurance that will challenge you every day to explore new opportunities for our clients worldwide. As a trusted advisor, you will tailor multinational insurance solutions for our global clients, empowering them to operate across borders with confidence and consistency. Partner with a dynamic, global team of experts, including underwriters, risk engineers, and analytics and claims professionals, to design, implement and service multinational insurance programs. This includes issuing timely policies, providing regulatory advice, sharing local knowledge, supporting efficient money movement capabilities and deploying large fronted limits. AIG Multinational professionals have the diverse skills and expertise necessary to deliver customized, compliant and seamless solutions that support our clients’ risk management objectives. With in-depth knowledge of local markets, practices and regulations, Multinational provides world-class insurance solutions and helps clients successfully navigate their cross-border risks, wherever in the world their businesses take them.
Role Summary
External broker and client facing role managing an assigned portfolio of Tier 2 Multinational programs working in partnership with product underwriters and distribution. This role supports all major Multinational lines of business.
About the role
What you need to know:
• Manage and oversee all aspects of the multinational service delivery for the assigned portfolio and be accountable for the multinational client experience. This would include:
o The proactive management and oversight of all multinational service activities, coordinating communication and project management across all internal and external stakeholders throughout the program lifecycle.
o Provide direction and guidance to all relevant stakeholders across Multinational Business Model and AIG Network to ensure appropriate design and effective delivery and service of assigned multinational programs.
o Provide multinational technical expertise to underwriters to ensure a compliant program structure and design, and adherence to all local regulatory requirements.
o Lead the promotion and adoption of the AIG Multinational End-to-End process, so that all parties understand and commit to roles, responsibilities and expected timelines, to provide an elevated service performance and deliver contract certainty.
o Ensure Multinational service fee discipline by utilizing available tools.
o Lead and manage the day-to-day service delivery to ensure the timely issuance of accurate local policy and invoice documentation and meet agreed program SLAs.
o Partner with Product Underwriters to manage the approval of facultative reinsurance panel participants and the collection of compliant reinsurance documentation for all assigned programs.
o Engage with multinational claims to ensure timely development of multinational claims bulletins / protocols and support on ad hoc program enquiries.
o Partner with underwriting to draft legal documentation for loss sensitive programs and obtain approval from AIG legal counsel.
o Monitor performance and escalate where necessary to ensure all agreed Multinational service SLAs are being met.
o Operate as the senior external service contact – working in collaboration with Product Underwriters and Distribution - and provide regular updates to the appointed broker (or client if direct) on program performance until fully implemented.
o Manage and partner with Distribution to coordinate periodic Multinational client/program stewardship meetings to be conducted in alignment and collaboration with underwriting and distribution.
• General:
o Provide multinational subject matter expertise and be an escalation point to support colleagues in respect of multinational program design, territorial information and multinational related problem solving as required.
o Accountable for contributing to the development, qualification, prospecting, and conversion of Multinational targets within assigned span of control.
o Support the profitable growth of the multinational portfolio by working in collaboration with product and distribution.

o Deliver structured internal and external Multinational training as applicable.

• Strong written & verbal communication and interpersonal skills
• Highly motivated and ability to work autonomously and on own initiative
• Ability to handle multiple priorities, delegate effectively and meet tight deadlines / SLAs
• Ability to clearly articulate ideas and influence outcomes
• Ability to motivate others to achieve common goal; proven record of being a team player
• Collaborative with the ability to build strong relationships with key internal and external stakeholders

JOB DESCRIPTION:

The Corporate Engineering (CE) organization is looking for an experienced and motivated individual to serve as Fire Protection Program Manager. This opportunity is for someone who wants to positively impact the organization in a meaningful role that applies advanced engineering knowledge and experience, combined with a disciplined project management approach, to deliver business solutions that span across divisions and regions. A part of Global Engineering Services (GES), Corporate Engineering exists to support Abbott’s businesses and help them drive sustainable growth and margin improvement. Corporate Engineering does this by planning, designing and deploying Facilities, Utilities & Infrastructure projects with excellence, by means of strong talent, best practices, resourcefulness, and experience. The GES/CE Fire Protection Program Manager role significantly contributes to that mission by leading and executing engineering activities across a broad set of responsibilities as outlined below.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

The Fire Protection Program Manager is an engineering professional who, working with little or no supervision, applies advanced scientific and engineering knowledge, mathematics and ingenuity to complete complex assignments related to the Fire Protection Engineering discipline. A Fire Protection Program Manager has full knowledge of other related disciplines beyond their own.

Specific responsibilities include but are not limited to:

Technical / Design: Benchmarks internally and externally. Independently executes or directs others in the design of facilities/utilities/infrastructure systems, by applying novel and proven engineering concepts and techniques. Performs detailed analysis, communicates across functions and disciplines, and serves as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) in design reviews.

Project Management: Identifies, plans and executes projects of varying degrees of complexity within engineering specialty, requiring custom risk-managed execution plans. Works with the client and cross-functional stakeholders to establish scope, cost and schedule on multiple projects. Independently performs economic analysis and feasibility studies related to complex and often multiple competing project alternatives. Manages multiple projects, often concurrently, maintaining project controls and reporting for scope, cost and schedule. Responsible for achieving the projects’ financial targets in support of business objectives.

Problem Solving / Innovation: Creates or coordinates design solutions for novel or complex problems focusing on cost-benefit, integrating regulatory needs (e.g. NFPA, Fire Code, Building Code, and Factory Mutual (FM) requirements) and operational needs (e.g. processes, materials, and people requirements). Structures studies to address cross-disciplinary and cross-functional issues and arrive at optimal solutions.

Organizational Interface: Mentors others by sharing technical knowledge and providing guidance. Where appropriate, provides tasks and project assignment opportunities for employee development and evaluates performance. Represents the organization as the prime technical contact, interacting with senior management and external parties on complex technical matters often requiring coordination between organizations. Conveys information effectively through formal and informal means including proposals, reports, design documentation, and presents to senior executive leadership. Submits articles for internal or external publication.

Compliance: Responsible for compliance with applicable Corporate and Divisional policies, procedures, and standards for Quality, Environmental, Health, Safety and Energy (EHS&E), Abbott Engineering Standards (AES), and other governance areas as applicable.

Additional Responsibilities May Include: Responsible for all matters pertaining the Fire Protection Engineering discipline as the global SME. Participates in internal cross-divisional teams to develop new, or revise existing, procedures and standards, and provides training. Directs the efforts of others such as engineers, technicians and outside resources. Crafts and submits Requests for Capital Expenditures (RCEs), safety/quality checklists, executive presentations, and projects financial reports. Resolves problems and crisis situations requiring assertive decisions and hands-on rapid implementation, by leveraging technical training and experience. Represents engineering on corporate and division initiatives.

EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE / SKILLS

B.S. degree in Fire Protection Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related discipline is required.

M.S. degree in Fire Protection Engineering is required if B.S. degree is not in Fire Protection Engineering.

Professional Engineer (PE) license is a plus.

Certifications: Certified Fire Protection Specialist (CFPS) is required.

Professional Affiliations: SFPE or NFPA membership is a plus.

Minimum of 12 years of experience in the design and deployment of fire protection solutions across building facilities and utilities systems.

Mastery of applicable codes, including NFPA (National Fire Protection Association), NEC (National Electrical Code), IFC (International Fire Code), IBC (International Building Code), and other local, national, and international regulatory requirements.

Experience with Fire Prevention/Detection/Suppression, Risk Management, and Loss Prevention.

Experience with fire protection systems including gas, water, pre-action, foam, and clean agent.

Experience with seismic bracing of fire protection systems.

Experience with underground fire mains, lead-ins, piping, and thrust blocks.

Experience with flammable liquids and hazardous materials storage, and maximum allowable quantities.

Experience with warehouses including flue spacing, high density storage, in-rack sprinklers, and commodity classifications.

Experience with Performance-Based Design (PBD) approach.

Experience with Life Safety and Egress analysis.

Experience with fire alarm, smoke detection, and smoke control systems.

Experience with Factory Mutual (FM) requirements, Plan Reviews, and inspection reports/responses.

Experience assessing the design and performance of fire protection and life safety systems on existing facilities, identifying gaps versus regulatory requirements and AES, and developing remediation plans.

Experience supporting construction and commissioning testing of fire protection and life safety systems.

Experience with fire/explosion protection on manufacturing processes is desired but not required.

Experience in regulated industries (e.g. medical device, pharmaceutical, or nutritional)

Excellent leadership, problem-solving, interpersonal, presentation, and communication skills.

Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-paced environment.

Proficiency in MS Project/Word/Excel/PowerPoint/Outlook, AutoCAD, SAP, Smartsheet, and Bluebeam.

Proven track record of successful execution throughout the entire project lifecycle: Feasibility –> Concept –> Design –> Construction –> Commissioning & Qualification –> Turnover –> Closeout.

Commitment to safety, quality and regulatory compliance.

The Opportunity 

This position works out of our Abbott Park, IL location within the GES Global Engineering Services Division.

The supervisor for Lake County Housekeeping is responsible for establishing and enforcing the policies and procedures for the department whether they be in the technical, personnel or administrative areas. The position is responsible for the work of between 10 – 20 housekeeping employees and directly supervises the activities of group leaders. The supervisor must plan work activities, provide training, tools and equipment for the housekeepers to safely, effectively preform their functions. The supervisor also coordinates work activities with other trade groups, engineers, and production personnel to maximize the efforts of Lake County. This position works out of Lake County and is second shift. You will work from 2:00 pm - 11:30 pm.

What You’ll Work On

Operating under the general guidance of the section manager, the duties of this position include but are not limited to:

Planning, organizing, staffing, training, directing, and controlling the housekeeping activities for Abbott Lake County.

More specific duties include the developing goals, policies, procedures, and programs to produce results in accordance with the corporate objectives as well as the objectives of individual customer divisions and departments.

The supervisor must understand and work successfully with customers who often have urgent and conflicting demands.

The supervisor must also determine requirements for new and replacement tools, provide training and job instructions, know safety rules and regulations and be sure the housekeeping team are trained on safe work practices.

This position requires the individual to seek out and stay current with new techniques, equipment and materials associated with the housekeeping field.

The supervisor must provide expert technical support for green, yellow and red radioactive environments, Bio level 1,2, and 3 environments as well as hazardous waste disposal guidelines.

The individual needs to be knowledgeable in entrance and exit procedures for controlled environments, cross contamination control procedures, microbial control procedures and aseptic cleaning techniques.

This position requires the individual to assure that all regulatory requirements are met and maintained to include FDA, GMP, OSHA, INTC, ALAC and ISO requirements to allow manufacturing of pharmaceutical, chemical, and diagnostic products to market.

The supervisor can also be called on to be a subject matter expert for housekeeping services when working with the FDA of other regulatory agencies.

Frequently, in addition to his/her more typical responsibilities, the incumbent will act in other assigned roles such as team leader or work on special interdivisional project teams and/or task forces, provide temporary support for departmental projects and be a temporary backup fo their manager. 

Required Qualifications

Associates Degree or the equivalent experience and formal post high school technical training such as executive housekeeping certification. Bachelor’s degree or working toward the completion is preferred.

5 years of industrial housekeeping work experience and at least two years’ experience as a leader.

Knowledge of all areas of housekeeping, including manufacturing cleaning and attestation experience.

5 years involvement in housekeeping/facility management.

Strong technical expertise to give direction to and gauge performance of the widely diverse technical services provided by this organization.
